findings.title: Retain admitted hidden diagnostic members in the upload
findings.problem: The capture upload invokes actions/upload-artifact@v4 without include-hidden-files:true. Current v4.4+ excludes hidden members by default. The unchanged reviewed transport no-follow inventory/export permits safe dot-prefixed files/directories inside retained raw evidence and publishes their exact identities in diagnostics metadata. A safely collected member such as visual-diagnostics/raw/evidence/.detail is silently omitted from the uploaded original, while sibling diagnostics.json/isolation files allow the upload to succeed. This breaks complete original-byte preservation and later manifest verification.
findings.source_fact: Official v4 README breaking changes and include-hidden-files input describe default hidden-member exclusion; inspected independently.
findings.fixed_transport_basis: capture_artifact.py _inventory/_publish/export_failure permit ordinary dot-prefixed names but reject unsafe components/types/links and enforce bounded no-follow export. capture_isolation.py collects only stopped/owned safe output into fresh upload destinations.
findings.bounded_fix: Enable include-hidden-files:true only for the admitted fixed transport capture roots. Keep current narrow run-owned paths; do not upload a checkout/temp parent or guessed roots. Add meaningful workflow retention assertion ensuring complete safe dot-member retention remains configured. No new evidence framework is needed.

findings.title: Produce safe metadata on the actual preflight CLI failure path
findings.problem: The real workflow runs the validate CLI before subject checkout. That CLI calls identity() directly, outside run() and its metadata finally. Invalid owner/rerun actor, ref, mode/subject or run identity raises there; capture is skipped and neither upload has an output path. The promised independent safe wrapper failure metadata is absent. The invalid-identity regression calls run() rather than the actual CLI/preflight path, so its retained-metadata assertions do not cover this real workflow behavior.
findings.bounded_fix: Use a common metadata-producing wrapper for validate-only and capture modes, and give the guard a step id. A successful guard has guard_passed:true and step_outcome:success while capture ok remains false/not attempted; failed guard retains safe failure metadata, false approvals and no capture root. Upload the capture metadata when present or the guard metadata otherwise. Keep guard failure before subject checkout/execution and never fall back to guessed capture paths. Add actual CLI/helper guard success/failure tests and workflow fallback-path assertions.
findings.parent_response: Parent agreed both findings and proposed exactly this small guard/common-wrapper/fallback repair after current managed precommit finishes; no corrected source has been reviewed in this v1 report.
